title: Case: A multi-parcel order arrives with one parcel still outstanding
context: An order consists of three separately tracked parcels. Two are received; the third must be traced by its own identifier.
initial_request: I received two of the three cartons for TG-3148. The missing carton is DL-2356-C. Please locate it; I am available tomorrow.

events.body: Order TG-3148 has parcels DL-2356-A, DL-2356-B and DL-2356-C. A and B have delivery scans; C has an inbound depot scan only. All three are required to complete the order.
I received two of the three cartons for TG-3148. The missing carton is DL-2356-C. Please locate it; I am available tomorrow.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Parcel trace team, Wrenfield Arc Logistics
acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the carrier to locate the missing parcel using its individual tracking ID.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Any team at Wrenfield Arc Logistics that appears in the history
acceptable_actions.summary: Ask the carrier to locate the missing parcel using its individual tracking ID. (asking that team to act or to route it to the team that owns it)

must_not: Closure is for the three-parcel count, not product quality or installation.
expected.reference_message: Please trace DL-2356-C specifically and arrange its remaining delivery. Do not mark TG-3148 complete using only the A and B scans.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-020: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation arrives by Email instead of Customer portal; replying on either channel is accepted. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
